title: Websim gets a new workspace
summary:
Websim gained a proper workspace, Pollinations UI gained a no-build browser bundle, and the shared interface got a quieter coat of paint.

Websim replaced its inline form with a responsive prompt-and-preview app, sign-in, and Save and Open actions for generated HTML. It now uses the user's token for generation, offers four model choices, keeps generated navigation within one HTML file, and has app-proxy routing under its pollinations.ai address.

A browser bundle exposes @pollinations/ui primitives and compositions through window.PollinationsUI, so pages can use the components without a build step. Existing ESM and CommonJS entries remain unchanged; React and ReactDOM are still loaded separately.

Enter, Playground, Model Monitor, and the React UI showcase adopted a single accent-token system, shared icons, softer borderless controls, and warmer dark-mode colors. A light/dark toggle initializes before paint to avoid a theme flash. Enter's models page also restores one-click copying of API IDs, while Model Monitor now judges health by the share of server errors even at low traffic.

highlights.title: Websim gets a workspace
highlights.text: Generate single-file HTML from a responsive prompt-and-preview interface, choose from four models, then save or open the result. Generation uses your Pollinations sign-in.

highlights.title: UI components without a build
highlights.text: Load `@pollinations/ui` as a browser bundle and use its primitives and compositions through `window.PollinationsUI`. Bring React and ReactDOM separately; no bundler required. [Explore the React UI](https://react.pollinations.ai).

highlights.title: One accent, two modes
highlights.text: Enter and Playground have a simpler shared look, with a light/dark toggle, new icons, and softer controls. The selected color mode is applied before the page paints, sparing you the brief flash of the wrong theme.
